newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper, aluminium stocks seen slightly down.
newsitem.headline: LME copper, aluminium stocks seen slightly down.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper and aluminium stocks will probably post modest falls overall on Tuesday, but some 5,000 tonnes of copper should arrive in Singapore from China soon, metal traders said.

Copper inventories may fall by 3,000 to 5,000 tonnes while aluminium, which posted a surprise increase of 6,900 tonnes last Friday, is expected to dip by between 1,000 to 4,000 tonnes when the LME stocks report is released at 0900 GMT.
"The stocks should be lower, but the aluminium figure last week was unexpected so it's a bit difficult to predict how the numbers will turn out," one Japanese dealer said.
At least 5,000 tonnes of copper is likely to arrive in Singapore soon from China, traders said.
"There's more tonnage moving to Singapore. Most of the stuff is coming from China," a European dealer said.

Traders estimated that there are between 15,000 to 20,000 tonnes of copper in Singapore warehouses which have not been placed on LME warrant and so do not show up in the exchange's stocks. They said holders of the material are betting prices will move higher.
Copper stocks in the LME warehouse in Singapore reached 8,625 tonnes on Friday, up 400 tonnes from last Tuesday, November 19, and sharply above the 1,450 tonnes in store last month.
Three month copper prices in the Far East were quoted at around US$2,215/20 a tonne at 0230 GMT, up from $2,204 a tonne in late trade in London on Monday, traders said.
Three month aluminium was priced here at 0230 GMT at around $1,508/13 a tonne against the late trade in London yesterday of $1,513 a tonne.
